To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women farmers in the Upper East of Ghana have access to credit from the RBs.
women farmers' access is determined by the socio-economic, technical and institutional variables.

women farmers' access and use of production credit from rural banks is influenced by their education level, application procedures, land ownership, income level, membership to economic association, savings, type and size of crop, interest rate and proximity to rural banks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which women farmers access credit and the factors that influence such access.
the extent of gender parity in credit supply by RB in Ghana and the socio economic, institutional and technical factors that have influence in access to credit by women farmers.
the extent of access to credit by rural women and the factors that influence such access in Ghana.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is gender parity in terms access to credit from the RBs in Ghana, and that women farmers are as likely to be credit worthy as men farmers.
the RBs in the Upper East Region of Ghana have been able to provide credit to women farmers at a ratio that is close to that of men.
there is gender parity in terms access to credit from the RBs by women and men farmers in Ghana.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paper has shown that women farmers have equal access to credit as men farmers in Ghana.
the paper provides evidence of gender parity in the provision of credit to women and men by financial institutions in developing countries.
women farmers in developing countries such as Ghana are able to gain access to credit from the financial institutions in general, and RBs in particular, in the same proportion as men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women in developing countries are as credit worthy as men and therefore deserve equal access to production credit.
there is need to address gender issues in the development of the rural and financial sectors of developing economies in order to enhance the development of the agriculture and rural sectors.
women in Ghana are not being discriminated against when it comes to accessing production credit from RBs.
